title: Moving-component lemma for an extremal subcanonical cluster
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes, meaning that at every singular closed point its completed local $k$-algebra is $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Write $h^i(X,F)=\dim_kH^i(X,F)$ for Zariski module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Assume that for every decomposition $X=A\cup B$ into nonempty reduced unions of components with no common component, $\dim_k\Gamma(A\times_XB,\mathcal O_{A\times_XB})\ge2$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $p_a(X)=1-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. Let $S\subseteq X$ be a subcanonical zero-dimensional closed subscheme, with ideal $I_S$ and splitting index $r(S)$ in [def-sfb-subcanonical-splitting-index]. Write $F_S=I_S\otimes\omega_X$, $V_S=H^0(X,F_S)$, $\ell(S)=\dim_k\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$ and $c(S)=2p_a(X)-\ell(S)-2\dim_kV_S$. Regard $V_S$ as a subspace of $H^0(X,\omega_X)$. Fix $R\in\mathbf N$. Assume $r(S)\le R$, $c(S)\le0$, and that for every subcanonical cluster $U\subseteq X$ with $r(U)\le R$ one has $c(S)\le c(U)$; among the clusters with $r(U)\le R$ and $c(U)=c(S)$ assume $\ell(S)\ge\ell(U)$. Also assume $0<\ell(S)<2p_a(X)-2$. For a general generically nonzero $s\in V_S$, let $S^*$ be its residual cluster [lem-sfb-subcanonical-residual-duality]. If some irreducible component $\Gamma$ of $X$ has both restriction images
$$\operatorname{im}(V_S\to H^0(\Gamma,\omega_X|_\Gamma)),\qquad \operatorname{im}(V_{S^*}\to H^0(\Gamma,\omega_X|_\Gamma))$$
of dimension at least two, then $\ell(S^*)=2$ and $h^0(X,F_{S^*})=p_a(X)-1$. More precisely there is a nonempty Zariski open subset of the affine space $V_S$ (in any basis) on which this implication holds for every generically nonzero $k$-point $s$.

proof.text: Put $g=p_a(X)$ and $V=V_S$. Residual duality gives finite-dimensionality and $h^0(X,\omega_X)=g$. Choose a generically nonzero section $a\in V$, which exists by subcanonicity. The empty cluster is subcanonical since $a$ is also a canonical section. Apply residual duality to the empty cluster and $a$, obtaining a cluster $D$ with $\ell(D)=2g-2$ and $h^0(X,F_D)=1$, hence $c(D)=0$. Here $F_\varnothing=\omega_X$, and its inclusion into $\omega_X$ (the identity) evaluates at $a$ to $a$, so $a$ lies in the evaluation image $F_D$ and $a\in H^0(X,F_D)$; thus its one-dimensional section space is generated by a section nonzero on every component. No partition with at least two blocks is admissible for this space: each block-supported subspace is zero. Therefore $r(D)=0$. If $c(S)=0$, maximality applied to $D$ gives $\ell(S)\ge2g-2$, contrary to the strict length hypothesis. Consequently $c(S)<0$. This uses the stated quantifier over all subcanonical clusters, including $D$.

proof.text: For each partition $\mathcal P$ of the finite component set, put $W_{\mathcal P}=\sum_{A\in\mathcal P}V_A\subseteq V$. Delete from $V$ every proper $W_{\mathcal P}$ and every kernel of restriction to a component. The latter kernels are proper since $V$ contains a generically nonzero section. There are only finitely many subspaces to delete. Their complement $\Omega$ is a nonempty Zariski open: after choosing a basis, choose a nonzero linear functional annihilating each proper subspace and multiply them; the product is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial. The field $k$ is infinite (a finite algebraically closed field is contradicted by $\prod_{b\in k}(T-b)-1$). The nonvanishing-direction node supplies a point where the product is nonzero. If no subspace is deleted, use the constant polynomial $1$. Here $\dim V\ge1$ by subcanonicity. Every $s\in\Omega(k)$ is generically nonzero.

proof.text: Fix $s\in\Omega(k)$ and form its residual $S_s^*$. The ideal inclusion $F_S\hookrightarrow\omega_X$, viewed as a local homomorphism, evaluates at $s$ to $s$. Thus $s$ belongs to both $F_S$ and $F_{S_s^*}$ inside $\omega_X$. For the union $U=S\cup S_s^*$ the ideal is $I_U=I_S\cap I_{S_s^*}$, so $s\in H^0(X,F_U)$ and $U$ is subcanonical. If $\mathcal P$ is admissible for $H^0(X,F_U)$, decompose $s$ into its block-supported summands there. They also belong to $V$, so $s\in W_{\mathcal P}$. The choice of $\Omega$ implies $W_{\mathcal P}=V$. This summation is injective: a relation between sections supported on disjoint blocks vanishes at every component generic point, hence is zero, since $X$ is reduced and $\omega_X$ is a line. Locally this says a coefficient in every minimal prime is zero. Therefore $\mathcal P$ is admissible for $V$, and $r(U)\le r(S)\le R$. The union is nonempty since it contains $S$.

proof.text: Apply the strict-negative residual-nesting node to $S$, $s$ and $U$. Its extremal inequalities are precisely the stated hypotheses, its strict inequality is Step 1, and its extra union hypotheses were proved in Step 3. It gives $S_s^*\subseteq S$ for every $s\in\Omega(k)$. No assertion about the splitting index of the residual or of an intersection is needed.

proof.text: Suppose some component $\Gamma$ has restriction image of $V$ of dimension at least two. Apply the moving-zero node with $L=\omega_X$, this $V$, and $Z=S$. Its hypotheses hold: the nodal dualizing module is invertible, $X$ is projective, reduced and pure one-dimensional, and finite-dimensionality was obtained in Step 1. Enlarge the finite collection of proper subspaces deleted in Step 2 by the finitely many subspaces furnished by that node. The same product-of-linear-functionals argument gives $s\in\Omega(k)$ outside them all. Hence $s$ vanishes at some closed point $x\in\Gamma\setminus|S|$.

proof.text: At this point $I_{S,x}=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, so $F_{S,x}=\omega_{X,x}$. In a local basis $e$ write $s_x=f e$. Every homomorphism $F_{S,x}\to\omega_{X,x}$ is multiplication by some $b\in\mathcal O_{X,x}$; evaluation at $s_x$ has image $(f)e$. By the definition of the residual in residual duality, $I_{S_s^*,x}=(f)$. Vanishing means $f\in\mathfrak m_x$, so $x\in|S_s^*|$, contradicting Step 4 and $x\notin|S|$. Thus every component restriction of $V$ has dimension at most one. The antecedent of the requested implication is therefore false for every generically nonzero $s$. Take the whole affine space $V$ as the required nonempty Zariski open; the implication, including both asserted numerical conclusions, holds on it.
